Article Title: DMK seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, rules out joint protests with Congress
Article Text:
DMK passes resolution demanding CEC's ouster, backs student protests

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: Escalating its attack on the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the DMK parliamentary party meeting on Saturday adopted a resolution demanding the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an investigation into his role. It also resolved to support the CJP's protest demanding Kumar's immediate removal and the withdrawal of the SIR, and condemned the police crackdown on youth protesters at Jantar Mantar.The DMK launched a sharp attack on its former ally, Congress, branding it a “habitual backstabber” that takes credit for others' work and betrays its allies. These positions were part of four resolutions adopted at the meeting chaired by DMK president and former chief minister M K Stalin at the party headquarters, Arivalayam.The party declared that it would not join any joint political action with Congress, accusing it of “double standards” for opposing the SIR at the national level while remaining silent on its selective impact across states. The DMK cited the deletion of more than 97 lakh voters from Tamil Nadu's electoral rolls during the revision exercise.The DMK also accused Vijay's TVK of double standards, citing reports linking voter deletions in Tamil Nadu to the party's electoral gains. It questioned TVK chief and chief minister C Joseph Vijay's refusal to criticise the BJP or Gyanesh Kumar and alleged an “under-the-table nexus” between the ruling party in Tamil Nadu and the BJP-led dispensation at the Centre.Seeking to restore public faith in democracy, DMK MPs, led by Stalin, will petition President Droupadi Murmu, pressing for two key demands.
Article Summary: DMK passes resolution demanding CEC's ouster, backs student protests. DMK launched a sharp attack on its former ally, Congress, branding it a “habitual backstabber” that takes credit for others' work and betrays its allies.

Article Title: Indian woman jailed over son’s fatal stabbing faces possible deportation from UK
Article Text:
Vickrum Digwa's mother Kiran Kaur was jailed for three years in July for assisting an offender

Kirpan argument sparks controversy

Police conduct under investigation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

An Indian woman jailed for helping her son after he fatally stabbed an 18-year-old student in Southampton could face deportation to India following her early release from prison, British authorities have indicated.According to new agency PTI, the UK Home Office said it would seek to deport foreign criminals at the earliest opportunity, although it did not refer specifically to Kiran Kaur, 53. Foreign nationals sentenced to at least 12 months in prison are generally considered for deportation, subject to exceptions and legal challenges.Kaur was sentenced to three years in prison in July for assisting an offender by removing the weapon used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill Henry Nowak on December 3, 2025. She is expected to be released early under a government scheme aimed at reducing overcrowding in British prisons.Digwa, 23, was sentenced to life imprisonment in June, with a minimum term of 21 years before he becomes eligible for parole.Both Kaur and her son have been granted permission to challenge their sentences, with their appeals scheduled to be heard by the UK Court of Appeal on November 5.The case drew widespread attention after Digwa sought to invoke a religious self-defence argument involving the kirpan, a ceremonial knife that Sikhs are legally permitted to carry in the UK.During Kaur’s sentencing, Justice William Mousley stressed that the kirpan was a symbol of religious faith and was not intended to be carried for offensive purposes. He said any use of the weapon in self-defence would have to be justified by circumstances involving great seriousness and urgency.The judge also criticised Kaur for removing the weapon rather than challenging her son’s actions and encouraging him to do the right thing.He acknowledged that she had experienced a difficult life in India before marrying and moving to the UK nearly 30 years ago. He said she had acted to protect her son rather than for personal gain and was unlikely to reoffend, while making clear that her actions warranted punishment.British Sikh organisations and parliamentarians subsequently condemned what they described as the misrepresentation of the kirpan, stressing that religious protection did not justify the violence in this case.The killing also triggered scrutiny of police conduct after body-worn camera footage showed officers handcuffing Nowak following Digwa’s allegations that he had been subjected to racism. Those allegations were subsequently rejected in court.The Independent Office for Police Conduct is investigating the officers’ handling of the incident amid allegations of “two-tier” policing, referring to claims that different communities were treated unequally.The case has heightened tensions in Southampton and the wider Hampshire and Isle of Wight area.Kaur’s potential deportation remains subject to the applicable immigration process, while the outcome of the appeals against her sentence and Digwa’s life term is awaited.
Article Summary: Kiran Kaur, 53, was jailed for three years in July for assisting an offender. She removed the weapon used by her son, Vickrum Digwa, to kill Henry Nowak. Home Office said it would seek to deport foreign criminals at the earliest opportunity.

Article Title: Middle East conflict: India pushes for 'resolution through dialogue and diplomacy' at UNSC
Article Text:
Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region

India flags attacks on commercial ships

Calls for de-escalation, protection of maritime routes

India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East, warning that the escalating hostilities pose a serious threat to regional stability and the safety of Indian nationals.Speaking at the UN Security Council ’s open debate on the Middle East, Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region, highlighting that around 10 million Indians live in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and contribute to their economies.He called for restraint and de-escalation, expressing concern over attacks on civilian infrastructure that have resulted in casualties, including the death of Indian citizen Mohammed Yusuf Ali in Riyadh.Harish said India stood in complete solidarity with the government and people of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty following the recent attacks.He also raised concerns over attacks on commercial shipping, including the India-flagged MV DP World Kaveri earlier this week and MT Petro Dolphin and MT Walthera last week.“All attacks on commercial shipping and merchant mariners are legally and morally indefensible,” he said, adding that several of the affected vessels had Indian seafarers whose safety and security remained India's direct responsibility.India reiterated the need for an immediate de-escalation of hostilities and a resolution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.Harish said attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must cease, stressing that freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways must be upheld in accordance with international law.He further added that focus on maritime security must not divert attention from the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. It condemned the October 7, 2023 attacks and reiterated its support for a negotiated two-state solution, the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803, and continued development and humanitarian assistance.v
Article Summary: India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East. Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it will be problematic if every citizen becomes a journalist as PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues already teeming with hordes of accredited reporters from registered media houses.Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists covering the protests and insisted on Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation. She said there must be a national protocol for police not to obstruct the professional work of any journalist who has an identity card from the employer.CJI Kant, however, struck a note of caution. “We must also keep one thing in mind. If everyone starts becoming a journalist, it will create problems for every other person,” he said. Justice Bagchi said, “It will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist. That is difficult. There are layers of protection for accredited journalists, those employed in registered media houses or whether they are freelance journalists, influencers or reel-makers.CJI Kant said, “The issue requires detailed examination — whether there should be a certain category of journalists to whom extra level of protection should be given.” Justice Bagchi added, “The Working Journalists Act makes classes among journalists. We must examine all that.”Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said in the present era of digital technology, any person with a mobile phone could claim to be an independent or freelance journalist when he/she would, in fact, be only making reels to garner popularity on social media to earn money by either presenting one-sided stories or sensationalising incidents.Mehta supported the contention that women journalists should not be harrassed, but argued that the same consideration should be extended to women police personnel as well.
Article Summary: PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues. Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists.

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah Thursday said not just Left-wing extremism but every trace of misery caused by five decades of Maoist violence must be wiped out. At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.Addressing the event via video conferencing, Shah said the programme, organised under 'seva sankalp abhiyan' to mark 25 years of PM Modi's 'seva and samarpan' (service), would help tribal people who had lost limbs or sensory abilities due to Naxal violence. Chhattisgarh govt organised it with welfare organisations such as Bhagwan Mahaveer Viklang Sahayata Samiti and Bharatiya Jain Sanghatana to provide prosthetic devices, wheelchairs, crutches and hearing aids.Held in Jagdalpur from Oct 5 to 7, the campaign benefited over 3,600 persons with disabilities, including over 1,570 from Bastar. Shah said Maoists' use of IEDs to maim innocent civilians for political objectives was a grave human rights violation.Though violent Naxalism was eliminated by the March 31, 2026 deadline, Shah said, the task would remain unfinished until govt healed victims' wounds, helped them stand and ensured they lived with dignity.Bastar was becoming vibrant again, he said, citing participation in Bastar Olympics and Bastar Pandum. Shah said 8,526 Naxalites had surrendered. Accounts had been opened for 7,328, reward money given to 1,620, incentives provided to 7,882, jobs offered to 455 and land allotted to 129. Another 4,014 beneficiaries had received houses under PM Awas Yojana, while over 2,308 tribal people had undergone skill training.A total of 6,763 ration cards had been issued, 2,808 families provided free electricity and work begun on 372 road projects. 48,526 people had received Aadhaar cards and 44 gram panchayats were recognised under 'Ilwad Panchayat Awards'.Twenty of the 50 security camps in Chhattisgarh will be converted into Shaheed Veer Gundadhur Seva Dera, providing public services, skill training and PDS benefits to nearby villages, Shah said. "The places where our security forces once sat to protect you will become the places where officials will lay the foundation for a developed Bastar," Shah added. tnn

Article Title: 'Ready to be detained': Dipke defiant ahead of Tiranga march in Delhi

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday claimed police personnel were keeping him under surveillance and said he could be detained overnight or on Friday morning, ahead of the outfit’s planned national flag-waving protest at Connaught Place.Addressing a press conference late Thursday, Dipke said he was prepared to go to jail for waving the Tricolour as the CJP called on supporters to gather at Central Park on Friday, despite the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) announcing a two-day closure of the venue.“Tomorrow, we will peacefully go and wave the Tiranga. As the citizens of this country, if you consider this to be a crime, then you are the biggest traitor,” Dipke said, as quoted by news agency PTI.“If we have to go to jail to wave the Tiranga in this country, then we are ready for it,” he added.Dipke questioned the decision to shut the park, saying the authorities could not close every location where the outfit might organise a demonstration. “Tomorrow, we will say that we will wave the Tiranga at 100 places. So you will shut down all 100 places?” he said.On X, Dipke alleged that undercover police personnel had surrounded his accommodation and were following him in a white Scorpio.The proposed march is part of the CJP’s campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The outfit has demanded Kumar’s resignation, alleging that more than 13 crore voters were deleted.Delhi Police has urged people to stay away from the gathering, citing prohibitory orders and saying Connaught Place is not a designated protest site. However, it said a limited group could be allowed to wave the national flag and sing the national anthem at a suitable location.The planned demonstration comes days after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to judicial custody for entering Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding Kumar’s resignation.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke claims police personnel are keeping him under surveillance. Dipke said he could be detained overnight or on Friday morning, ahead of the outfit’s planned national flag-waving protest at Connaught Place.

American singer Mary Millben has alleged that billionaire George Soros is funding protests in India, reiterating her support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and targeting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke.In a video message, Millben claimed that Soros and people associated with him were financing protests against conservative leaders across the world, urging young Indians to rally behind Modi and counter what she described as “chaos and destruction”.“The name is George Soros and that whole machine of people are constantly funding a lot of these protests and chaos that's breaking out across the world,” she said.The remarks follow Millben's October 14 post on X, in which she alleged that Dipke and the CJP were receiving funding from US-based donors opposed to Modi. She had also called on young Indians to organise a peaceful counter-movement against the protests, framing them as an attempt to create disruption in the country.Abhijeet Dipke had hit back at Millben on X, questioning the involvement of foreign nationals in India's domestic affairs.‘We don't need outsiders interfering in our country's affairs,’ he said.Mary Millben further criticised Rahul Gandhi and Dipke, accusing them of creating disruption without offering solutions.Comparing the protests with movements in the United States, she cited the civil rights movement led by Martin Luther King Jr. as an example of peaceful mobilisation that brought legislative change.“Your voice should want to bring about change that unifies the country and that works with everyone to find the best solution for the people that you serve,” she said.Millben also urged Dipke to engage directly with the government rather than continue the protests, saying he should use his ability to mobilise people constructively. She argued that movements lacking clear objectives would eventually fade, while those delivering meaningful change would be remembered.She concluded by calling on young Indians to organise peaceful demonstrations in support of PM Modi, describing such mobilisation as a counter-movement based on patriotism, peace and unity.
Article Summary: Mary Millben alleges that billionaire George Soros is financially backing protests in India with the intention of undermining Prime Minister Modi's government. NEW DELHI: The All India Students' Association (AISA) on Friday claimed that its national president Neha Bora was being detained at Delhi's RK Puram police station.Advocate Supantha Sinha, who met Bora at the police station along with other lawyers, said she was taken into custody around 5pm, but her location was disclosed only around 10.30pm. Article Title: SIR protests: Opposition has found common ground. But can it stay united?
Article Text:
Members of INDIA bloc at high-tea hosted at Rahul Gandhi's residence in Delhi (File photo)

Delhi Police detained more than 3,000 people attempting to reach Jantar Mantar for the protest.

What Rahul Gandhi said after CJP leaders were arrested.

From NEET protests to Jantar Mantar 2.0

Police personnel restrain Congress leader Rahul Gandhi during a protest near PMO

The SIR and 'vote chori' campaign

Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with student leader Neha Bora, during INDIA bloc's anti-CEC protests.

AISA president Neha Bora calls for a united fight against the BJP

Opposition closes ranks

From Mamata to Kejriwal, opposition leaders back arrested CJP leaders

The counter

Together, but still separate?

Dipke reiterated that CJP will always remain a pressure group.

Has the opposition finally found its feet?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: "All protests are one," Congress leader Rahul Gandhi declared on Wednesday as opposition parties rallied behind two Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders sent to judicial custody following demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke welcomed Rahul's support, thanking the Congress leader for standing with the arrested protesters.Just days ago, that was hardly how things looked on Delhi's streets, where Congress and CJP appeared to be competing for space and prominence while leading separate campaigns against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Congress-led INDIA bloc was organising its own demonstrations, while CJP, which had mobilised thousands of protesters in July, prepared separately for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10.AAP, TMC and the Left were willing to join CJP's agitation, but Congress kept its distance. Their objective was the same, but they were fighting for it separately. Many wondered why.On October 10, the Delhi police enforced an unprecedented clampdown in the national capital to prevent mobilisation for CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0. Thousands of protesters were dragged on the streets and detained.Such was the intensity of police action that the CJP stir could not even take off.The top CJP leaders were arrested from a plane on landing in Delhi, drawing flak from some quarters for their easy “surrender.” Several political parties stood with the cockroaches, but the Congress stayed away.The trigger for greater unity came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested on October 14 following their attempt to protest at Jantar Mantar by waving the Tricolour. Rahul Gandhi came out in open support for first time, and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke thanked him.The dynamics now seem to be changing, with Congress and CJP more willing to support each other, if not formally join forces. But why? Have both sides realised the limitations of organising separate protests for the same cause? Let's decode this shift.In June, when CJP protested against the NEET paper leak and demanded the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Congress stayed away. Rahul was leading his own programme, Chhatron Ki Goonj, on similar issues.AAP, the Left and social activists joined CJP at Jantar Mantar. The movement gained momentum with Sonam Wangchuk and AISA leader Neha Bora sitting on an indefinite fast. But Congress continued to stay away.On July 20, Delhi Police launched a major operation against students and young protesters who had reached the capital on CJP's call. The next day, Rahul joined the agitation and staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, shifting Congress's focus from its own campaign.However, with the government entering negotiations with CJP and later accepting its demands, including Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, Congress was left on the sidelines.The anti-paper leak protests were perhaps a wake-up call for political parties, especially Congress, as large numbers of young people mobilised behind CJP. Prime Minister Modi subsequently turned to Instagram to reach out to Gen Z, while other parties were left to rethink their youth outreach.Congress had been at the forefront of the 'vote chori' campaign, with Rahul holding press conferences highlighting alleged discrepancies in electoral rolls. The party also led a yatra in Bihar ahead assembly elections in the state.The momentum gradually faded, before an Indian Express report on differences within the Election Commission over SIR returned the issue to centre stage. CJP took up the issue, organising a Mumbai rally and setting an October 10 deadline for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, failing which it called for Jantar Mantar 2.0.Congress and the INDIA bloc also stepped up their campaign, announcing a six-point action plan that included an October 6 street protest. With CJP's mobilisation approaching, INDIA bloc leaders returned to the streets for four consecutive days until October 9, perhaps keen not to be left on the sidelines again. But on October 10, the D-day of CJP mobilisation, Rahul was in Chennai and the Congress stayed away.Another change had taken place between July and October. Civil society groups and activists associated with CJP's earlier movement were now actively participating in the INDIA bloc's SIR campaign.The most prominent was Neha Bora, national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA). During the October 12 march towards the Supreme Court, Rahul walked with his hands on the shoulders of Bora and Priyanka Gandhi, with senior opposition leaders following behind.The moment appeared to signal Congress's willingness to bring prominent youth protest faces into its campaign. Political analyst Uday Chandra explained the significance of this shift."Congress under RG recognises that youth-led protests have mobilised ordinary people beyond the reach of traditional party organisations. Neha Bora is an interesting bridge between these worlds, though she leads AISA, a Left student organisation, not CJP," Chandra said.He also pointed to a shift in student politics. "What I find most interesting is that AISA and NSUI are fighting together today. This wasn't the case in the past," he said.As CJP leaders' arrests drew support across party lines, this cooperation was no longer limited to student organisations.The support for CJP has not come from Congress alone.TMC leader Mamata Banerjee condemned the arrests as an attempt to intimidate young protesters. Party MP Abhishek Banerjee accused the BJP of arresting people for waving the national flag, calling it "BJP's new Pakistanified Bharat". Mahua Moitra also expressed solidarity.AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal questioned whether waving the Tricolour could be a crime. DMK president MK Stalin offered legal assistance to the two CJP leaders, while NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Aaditya Thackeray condemned the arrests.The Left maintained its support. Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan criticised the arrests. CPI general secretary D Raja called the police action undemocratic and said his party's student and youth organisations would intensify their campaign for the right to protest at Jantar Mantar.The growing opposition presence was visible beyond Delhi. On Thursday, Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which had stayed away from earlier anti-CEC demonstrations, joined a Congress-led INDIA bloc protest in Chennai. TVK had joined the alliance on October 3; leaders from VCK, MDMK and other partners also participated.More protests may follow. NCP(SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande said Rahul had asked INDIA bloc leaders to be prepared for further demonstrations at 24 hours' notice.These parties have their own priorities and have not always followed the same protest programme. Yet, from Delhi to Chennai, more opposition leaders are speaking out on the same issue. CJP and the INDIA bloc, however, have not announced any joint protest programme.The BJP has rejected the opposition's allegations, accusing rivals of using street demonstrations to question democratic institutions after electoral defeats.On October 10, BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad said: "We are not opposed to protests, but you have weaponised street protests because of your electoral defeats."BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra also questioned whether events at Jantar Mantar represented the larger picture of India. The Election Commission has denied allegations of political bias in electoral-roll revision.For CJP, opposition support presents an opportunity and a challenge. The group has built its identity as an independent youth-led movement, but the detention of its leaders and criticism of its leadership raise questions about sustaining the agitation without established parties.Uday Chandra cautioned against reading too much into the cooperation."There is certainly a convergence of interests at this moment, but we should not mistake that for anything akin to a formal alliance. The police crackdown and detention of protesters have created a common cause for the CJP and the INDIA bloc," Chandra said.He noted that CJP's independence has been central to its youth appeal and that its leaders have criticised the opposition in the past.Political commentator Sugata Srinivasaraju questioned whether CJP had established a support base strong enough to sustain a larger movement. He warned that becoming an extension of Congress could cost it its independent identity. Nor was it clear whether CJP would lead any joint campaign or give way to a larger party.For Congress, CJP's ability to mobilise young people is attractive. But could closer cooperation undermine the independence that made those movements appealing in the first place?Chandra warned: "The autonomy of these youth movements is precisely what makes them politically significant. If parties or their student unions undermine that autonomy, the movement may splinter amidst loud bickering, and can even fizzle out following discord."CJP founder Dipke has maintained that the group will remain an independent pressure group, despite sharing the opposition's demand for Kumar's removal.The INDIA bloc has struggled to present a united front since its inception. Disagreements over leadership, seat-sharing and political priorities have divided parties, and Congress has faced criticism over its lack of efforts to keep the coalition together.The protests against the CEC have offered a different picture: common ground emerging from demonstrations rather than electoral negotiations. Differences remain, however. AAP and DMK, once part of the INDIA bloc, are still not ready to join hands with Congress.But does a greater presence on the streets mean the opposition has finally found its feet?Sugata Srinivasaraju disagreed that the opposition had been missing in action. Parties, he argued, had always been active, even if street demonstrations had recently become more frequent."More frequent protests do not necessarily mean a more effective opposition. Without planning, structure and a clear strategy, such demonstrations can become counterproductive, with little lasting political impact," he said.He also questioned what the prominence of youth leaders from outside Congress said about its leadership."It also reflects the opposition's inability to lead itself and absence of strong, charismatic leaders of its own. By bringing in faces from youth-led movements, it is, in a way, acknowledging that leadership gap. But there is a risk that leaders like Neha Bora could lose their independent identity within a larger political organisation, much like what happened with Kanhaiya Kumar," he said.The coming together of opposition parties has changed the picture on the streets, but questions remain over whether they can sustain protests, develop new leaders and turn a common cause into a coordinated campaign.For years, the question has been: Where is the opposition? With parties now finding common ground after months of differences, could that question finally have an answer?
Article Summary: Congress and CJP appeared to be competing for space and prominence while leading separate campaigns against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The trigger for greater unity came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested on October 14 following their attempt to protest at Jantar Mantar.

NEW DELHI: Bihar MLA Anant Singh made a shocking claim that he had got “nine people murdered” while supporting Nitish Kumar . The JD(U) leader Singh made the remark during an interview with news agency IANS while describing his long association with the party supremo.Recalling his sacrifices for Nitish Kumar, Mokama MLA claimed: “Who has made as many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then. He used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered,” Singh said.However, later the leader clarified that his remarks was misinterpreted and that he was referring to the killing of nine of his associates, not claiming that he had arranged their murders.Singh said the nine people killed was his personal loss that he suffered after aligning himself with Nitish Kumar and abandoning Lalu Yadav . Singh also claimed that he was shot at during that period. He also recalled that his father died after suffering a heart attack.According to Singh, the killings took place just days after a meeting with Nitish Kumar. He said that although Lalu Prasad Yadav had advised him against attending the meeting, he went ahead and had Nitish Kumar weighed against silver coins.Singh maintained that he had cited these incidents to explain the sacrifices he made while supporting Nitish Kumar. He said his remarks had been taken out of context and denied claiming that he had arranged the murders.The controversy comes amid tensions within the Janata Dal (United) over its choice ofNeeraj Kumar as the party's candidate for the Patna Graduates' constituency MLC election.Singh has criticised the decision, alleging that Neeraj Kumar had previously opposed him and questioning his contributions to the party. He has insisted that his disagreement is with the candidate selection and not with Nitish Kumar himself.In the same interview, Singh said, “I am a devotee of Nitish. I am not challenging anyone.”Singh also recounted how Nitish Kumar had helped secure an assembly election ticket for his brother by speaking to Lalu Prasad Yadav, who was then allied with Nitish. Singh said he continued to support Nitish after the two leaders parted ways and eventually left Lalu Prasad's camp to join forces with Nitish.Known locally as 'Chhote Sarkar', Singh has continued to oppose Neeraj Kumar's candidature despite reported efforts by senior JD(U) leaders to resolve the disagreement.
Article Summary: JD(U) leader Anant Singh made the remark while describing his long association with the party supremo. Singh later clarified that his remark was misinterpreted. Remarks amid dispute over MLC candidate Neeraj Kumar. Singh has insisted that his disagreement is with the candidate selection and not with Nitish Kumar.

Article Title: 'Hope better sense prevails': SC flags traders' livelihood concerns as Delhi braces for CJP's Tiranga march

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined an urgent hearing on a plea challenging the New Delhi Municipal Council's decision to shut Central Park in Connaught Place ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's ( CJP ) proposed ‘Lehra do Tiranga’ protest, saying it hoped “better sense will prevail” among all concerned.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it was conscious of the difficulties that a closure could cause to small shopkeepers and their families, while observing that the right to protest, the need to maintain law and order and the livelihood of traders were interconnected issues.“We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship and difficulty entire families will face,” the bench said.Justice Bagchi said the court could intervene if the restrictions resulted in business losses, adding that it would consider exercising its constitutional jurisdiction if required."If there's loss of business, we will exercise our powers under Constitutional jurisdiction. Let's cross that bridge when it comes," Justice Bagchi said.During the hearing, the petitioner's lawyer submitted that the NDMC had issued directions late Thursday night to close Central Park, effectively preventing businesses from operating in the area. The civic body had announced that the park would remain closed to the public on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons.The bench indicated that the plea could be listed on October 26 or 27.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has called on citizens to gather at Central Park with the national flag at 5 pm on Friday, alleging that party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were jailed for unfurling the Tricolour. The party has said it will proceed with the march despite the closure of the park and security restrictions.In a post on X, Dipke defended the party's protests, rejected allegations that it was promoting anarchy and accused the government of restricting democratic rights."Businesses do not suffer because of peaceful protests. They suffer when the govt decides to shut down an entire city, suspend internet services and restrict the movement of its own citizens and turn the city into a war-zone.""Since its inception, the Cockroach Janta Party has maintained that we will always follow Mahatma Gandhi’s path of peace and non-violence, and we have stood by that commitment. We have organised protests in Mumbai, Pune, Jaipur, Lucknow, Bengaluru and Nagpur, and every single one of them has been peaceful. I was personally assaulted in Jaipur, but even then, I chose not to retaliate because responding to violence with violence goes against everything we believe in. We would rather exercise the rights guaranteed to us by the Constitution, drafted under the leadership of Dr. BR Ambedkar, than resort to physical force. Our strength comes from our commitment to constitutional values, and no amount of provocation will make us abandon them.""Despite this, there are constant attempts to portray us as anarchists simply because we refuse to remain silent. But demanding answers from the govt is not anarchy, protesting against injustice on the streets is not anarchy, and questioning those who hold public office is certainly not anarchy. These are the most fundamental expressions of democracy. The very party that is in power today spent decades organising protests, taking to the streets and questioning the governments of the day when it was in opposition. Had the same restrictions, intimidation and police crackdowns been used against them, many of those who occupy positions of power today might never have reached where they are. It is deeply hypocritical to celebrate protests as a democratic right when you are in opposition and treat the same act as a threat to public order when you come to power."ALSO READ: ‘No one called Mahatma Gandhi African’: Sanjay Raut slams order against actor Imran Khan "We are not asking for privileges or special treatment. We are simply asking to exercise the rights that belong to every citizen of this Republic, irrespective of which party is in power. So let us fulfil our duty as citizens of this country by questioning those we elect, demanding accountability and speaking up whenever we witness injustice.""A govt that has been elected by the people is bound to listen to the people, not silence them. Democracy does not end once the votes have been counted."The proposed demonstration comes amid a standoff between the CJP and Delhi Police over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The CJP had announced the march after Das and Ranka were arrested for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, and raising slogans demanding Kumar's resignation. They were subsequently remanded to five days of judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail.Dipke has urged political parties and civil society organisations to set aside ideological differences and join the demonstration."I request all political parties and civil society groups to rise above ideology and come together. If the right to vote is not saved, democracy will not be saved," Dipke said at a press conference on Thursday.He also questioned the scale of voter deletions during the SIR exercise and alleged that the revisions could affect electoral outcomes."The margin of victory in 2024 was just 2 per cent. Over 13 crore voters deleted -- around 14 percent," he said."Where 2 per cent is deciding the election, you are deleting 13 crore votes. What is this if not a setting?" he added.The CJP has alleged that the government is shielding Kumar from scrutiny. These allegations have not been established by the court.Delhi Police has said Connaught Place is not a designated site for protests and that demonstrations can be held at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permissions."Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a designated protest site. Protesters can hold demonstrations at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permission," a senior police officer said.Security has been tightened around Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar, with several companies of paramilitary personnel stationed in the national capital. Police are deploying personnel at strategic locations, erecting barricades and regulating the movement of protesters and commuters to prevent any untoward incident.The NDMC issued its closure notice on Thursday, stating that Central Park would remain shut on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons. The decision came a day after the CJP announced its proposed march at the park, located in the centre of Connaught Place's inner circle.The party's agitation began in Mumbai on October 2 and subsequently moved to Delhi. On October 10, a planned demonstration at Jantar Mantar was met with a police crackdown, with Dipke, Das and Ranka detained at the airport after arriving from Mumbai. Opposition leaders, activists and students were also detained during protests in the capital.On October 13, CJP members entered the barricaded Jantar Mantar site carrying the national flag and were detained.Opposition parties and student organisations have separately held demonstrations against the SIR exercise and demanded accountability from the Election Commission. INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission headquarters on October 6 and were stopped by police barricades. Opposition leaders later met President Droupadi Murmu on October 9 to raise their concerns.The CJP has since framed its proposed Connaught Place march as a campaign for voting rights and the constitutional right to protest, setting up another confrontation over the restrictions imposed on demonstrations in central Delhi.
Article Summary: Supreme Court declines urgent plea against Central Park closure ahead of ’s Tiranga march. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has called on citizens to gather at Central Park with the national flag at 5 pm on Friday. The party has said it will proceed with the march despite the closure of the park.

Article Title: 'Verify before she vilifies': India rejects UN rapporteur's claims on youth protests
Article Text:
India rejects UN rapporteur Gina Romero’s claims on youth protests

NEW DELHI: India has rejected allegations by UN special rapporteur Gina Romero that young people in the country face retaliation and stigmatisation for discussing mental health and gender justice, calling the claims based on anonymous and unverified submissions.Speaking at an interactive dialogue with Romero during the 81st session of the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee, India’s first secretary Anuj Swarup questioned the evidence cited in her report on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and association.“Yet, the special rapporteur, Ms Gina Romero, asserts that young people in India face retaliation or stigmatisation for discussing mental health or gender justice, though merely citing unnamed submissions in the footnote. This level of arbitrary report writing is precisely the reason that the United Nations and its institutions have lost credibility,” Swarup said.“A sweeping charge against the world's largest youth population resting on anonymous and unverified claims is not evidence. It is hearsay, dressed up as a UN report, and my delegation rejects it outright,” he added.Swarup said India’s Constitution guarantees freedom of assembly, association, speech and expression under Article 19, with these rights protected by an independent judiciary, a free press and the National Human Rights Commission.He also cited young people’s participation in political movements and engagement with senior government leaders as evidence of civic space in the country.“In which repressive state does a satirical youth party question the government, marches on the capital, and then sits across the table with senior national leaders?” he asked, referring to a youth-led political movement mentioned in Romero’s report.“Chair, a mandate holder who relies on anonymous inputs to generalise for 1.4 billion people does a disservice to the very mandate she holds. We urge this special rapporteur to verify before she vilifies and to bring the required rigour and fairness in her reports,” he said.The remarks come amid heightened scrutiny of the government’s handling of youth protests, including demonstrations over alleged irregularities in public examinations and the recent anti-SIR stir.Romero had alleged in posts on X on October 10 that peaceful youth protesters in India faced excessive force and arbitrary detention. She also claimed that more than 2,500 protesters had been sent to remote detention centres without legal support, with some allegedly tortured or sexually assaulted. She further alleged that phones had been seized, protest-related material deleted and internet access restricted.These allegations were made by Romero and were not independently established in the information provided by India’s statement.India, meanwhile, defended its response to student protests over examination irregularities, saying the government had engaged with young people and taken steps to address exam fraud.Swarup said Parliament had amended the Public Examinations Act, doubled punishments for paper leaks, overhauled the examination system and created fast-track courts in every state to prosecute exam fraud.He also pointed to the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue, saying more than five million young people had participated this year and helped shape national priorities through direct engagement with the Prime Minister.
Article Summary: India rejects UN rapporteur Gina Romero’s claims on youth protests in the country. India calls the claims based on anonymous and unverified submissions. Romero had alleged that peaceful youth protesters in India faced excessive force and arbitrary detention. She also claimed that more than 2,500 protesters had been sent to remote detention centres without legal support.

SRINAGAR: A purported video of a senior J&K IAS officer, Kumar Rajeev Ranjan, allegedly using abusive language against a junior woman colleague at a virtual meeting has triggered an outcry, an inquiry, an NCW notice and calls for the senior bureaucrat to be shunted out.In the video from Wednesday’s meeting, Ranjan, secretary of labour and employment department, is heard telling Beenish Wani, a J&K Administrative Service (JKAS) officer, “shut up” and “bloody shit”.CM Omar Abdullah decried Ranjan’s behaviour and wrote to chief secretary (CS) Atal Dulloo for action. It issued a circular asking all officials to “maintain the highest standards of integrity, devotion to duty, discipline and conduct becoming of a public servant”.The action came as National Commission for Women (NCW) took suo motu cognisance of the video and its chairperson, Vijaya Rahatkar, wrote to chief secretary Dulloo pressing for an impartial inquiry, to be followed by appropriate disciplinary and legal action if the allegations are established.NCW also called for safeguards against workplace harassment and professional retaliation, along with protection and support for Wani. I would have put him on a plane and sent him back,” Farooq said.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of home affairs (MHA) on Friday sought reports from the Punjab government on multiple recent incidents involving the deaths of men in cases linked in allegations to the state's drug problem.The details demanded were linked to the killing of anti-drug crusader Parwinder Singh alias Jhota in Mansa, the fatal attack on Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur and the reported suicide of Gulzar Singh, who had allegedly raised concerns over the availability of synthetic drugs.In one of the letters to Punjab chief secretary,MHA referred to the killing of Parwinder Singh on October 13 and described him as “reportedly a crusader against rampant sale and abuse of narcotics and psychotropic drugs in Punjab”. The ministry noted that protests had taken place in the state following his killing and asked the state government to furnish a “comprehensive factual report” on the incident and the steps taken in the case.Jhota was known for his opposition to drug abuse and alleged drug peddling in Punjab.Read more: Punjab Bandh after activist Parminder Singh Jhota’s killing - Trucks on roadside, barricades on all roads to Mansa The ministry also sought details of action taken by the state government on the Union government's Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029), which Union home minister Amit Shah had shared with the Punjab chief minister on August 10, 2025.The document outlines measures to advance the objective of a drug-free India, including setting up or restructuring a dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), mandatory financial investigations, outcome-oriented reviews under the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism, strengthening prosecution and courts dealing with cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, appointing nodal officers and acting against transnational drug networks.Meanwhile, in a second letter, the MHA sought a detailed report on the attack on Bikramjit Singh and two others, Nishan Singh and Gurmukh Singh, in Mari Panwan village in Gurdaspur district. Bikramjit died in the incident, while the other two were critically injured.According to local residents, Bikramjit and his companions had objected to alleged drug peddling in the village before they were attacked with sharp-edged weapons. Residents alleged that the assault was linked to their opposition to drug-related activities and said fear of retaliation had discouraged people from reporting alleged drug peddling.Bikramjit’s relatives disputed the police account that the murder followed a scuffle between two groups over a mobile phone. Police have denied a drug-related motive and said an FIR had been registered, with an investigation underway to identify and arrest the accused.Read more: Another Punjab man killed after opposing drug sales; police cite phone dispute In the third letter, the MHA sought a report on the reported suicide of Gulzar Singh on September 8. The letter described him as the father of a young person with substance dependence and said reports alleged that, before his death, he had questioned the availability of synthetic drugs in his area and levelled allegations against a Punjab government minister.The letter further referred to allegations that Gulzar Singh had faced systematic harassment and pressure from the local village panchayat, which purportedly drove him to take his own life. Citing public distress and potential law-and-order implications, the ministry asked the state government to submit a detailed report on the incident.The three letters, dated October 16, were addressed to the Punjab chief secretary and copied to the state's director general of police.Meanwhile, home minister Amit Shah, earlier in the day himself raised concerns over the drug-related crises in the state. NEW DELHI: Delhi traders have urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to intervene over losses running into crores of rupees allegedly caused by the CJP-called October 10 protest, accusing the organisers of being ignorant of ground realities and seeking compensation from those responsible for the disruption.In a representation, the Automotive Parts Merchants Association (Regd.), Delhi, said customers stayed away from markets for four to five days before and after the protest call, causing heavy losses to businesses.The association said October, November and December were crucial for traders because of the festive season, including Navratri, Dhanteras and Diwali. It warned that repeated disruptions during this period could threaten the livelihoods of shopkeepers and their employees.The association urged the authorities to ensure a transparent assessment of the losses suffered by shopkeepers following the October 10 protest and recover full compensation from the principal organisers and participants responsible, rather than place the financial burden on traders already struggling with lost business.It said shop earnings supported traders' families and employees, while covering shop rents, children's education and medical expenses for elderly parents.The trade body also raised concerns about protests held without basic emergency arrangements, including ambulances, fire services and first aid, warning that the lack of safeguards could lead to serious accidents.It appealed to the Supreme Court, the Delhi High Court, the Central Government and the Prime Minister to intervene. It also sought restrictions on future protests or marches that bring normal life and commercial activity in Delhi to a standstill.ALSO READ: 'I am alone': CJP's Dipke argues with cops during detention ahead of Tiranga march - watch The appeal comes amid heightened security in Connaught Place ahead of a proposed Tiranga Yatra by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke.Delhi Police teams visited the residence where Dipke was staying and served him a notice stating that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force in and around Connaught Place. The notice said the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) had not granted permission for the proposed march and warned that proceeding without permission could invite legal action.Police clarified that waving the national flag was not illegal, but holding an unauthorised march or gathering a crowd in violation of restrictions could lead to action. Dipke was also reminded of the rules governing the respectful use of the national flag.The NDMC announced that Central Park in Connaught Place would remain closed to the public on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons. Traffic movement on some roads around the area was also expected to be affected from 3 pm on Friday.Dipke rejected claims that demonstrations disrupt business, arguing that administrative restrictions were responsible for causing hardship to traders and residents."Businesses do not suffer because of peaceful protests. They suffer when the govt decides to shut down an entire city, suspend internet services and restrict the movement of its own citizens and turn the city into a war-zone. Since its inception, the Cockroach Janta Party has maintained that we will always follow Gandhi’s path of peace and non-violence, and we have stood by that commitment."He also argued that demanding answers from the government was not anarchy and said an elected administration was bound to listen to citizens rather than silence them.

India’s patriotic public and the Bharatiya Janata Party will never allow any attempt to weaken the country’s democratic system to succeed,” he added.Nabin’s remarks came a day after activist Prashant Bhushan, addressing a press conference in Delhi alongside student leaders and activists, said that expressing “disaffection” against a government was not a crime in a democracy and that the struggle was now “really for a regime change.”“The government alleges that the opposition wants a regime change... We are currently fighting to ensure that elections are conducted properly. But if this kind of brutality continues, there will certainly be a regime change,” Bhushan told reporters.AISA president Neha Bora, another prominent face of the ongoing anti-SIR protests in Delhi, also "thanked" Bangladesh for "showing us the way.""The Gen Z movement we are seeing everywhere in this country first started in Bangladesh and congratulations to you for showing us the way and extending solidarity to the young people of this country," Bora is heard saying in the 39-second video clip shared by BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari.The remarks came against the backdrop of student-led movements in neighbouring Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka that led to the ouster of incumbent governments.
Article Summary: The BJP chief accused the opposition of seeking to seize power “at any cost” He described the alleged plot as part of the “Urban Naxals’” agenda. Article Title: ‘Refrain from actions prejudicial to citizens’ rights’: Delhi Police notice to CJP's Abhijeet Dipke ahead of Tiranga march
Article Text:
Cops at Dipke's home, serve notice barring him from holding Tiranga march

Dipke defends peaceful protests, accuses government of curbs

Central Park closed, traffic restrictions announced

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Friday served a notice to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, warning him against holding the proposed Tiranga Assembly at Central Park in Connaught Place without permission from the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC).The notice stated that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force in the Connaught Place area. Police warned that proceeding with the proposed gathering despite the restrictions could invite legal action.The notice also directed Dipke to "Refrain from action prejudicial to rights of citizen, traders, commuters, others."According to the notice, waving the national flag was not prohibited, but holding an unauthorised march and assembling a crowd in the restricted area would violate the orders. Police also cautioned Dipke to follow the Flag Code while displaying the national flag.The CJP activist was served the notice at his residence in the Jhandewalan area in the presence of a Delhi Police official, ANI reported. The move came amid heightened security arrangements in and around Connaught Place ahead of the proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest.Earlier, Dipke rejected allegations that the CJP's demonstrations promoted disorder, arguing that demanding accountability from those in power was a democratic right.In a post on X, he accused the authorities of disrupting businesses and restricting citizens' movement through administrative measures, including shutting down areas and suspending internet services."Businesses do not suffer because of peaceful protests. They suffer when the govt decides to shut down an entire city, suspend internet services and restrict the movement of its own citizens and turn the city into a war-zone. Since its inception, the Cockroach Janta Party has maintained that we will always follow Gandhi’s path of peace and non-violence, and we have stood by that commitment. We have organised protests in Mumbai, Pune, Jaipur, Lucknow, Bengaluru and Nagpur, and every single one of them has been peaceful. I was personally assaulted in Jaipur, but even then, I chose not to retaliate because responding to violence with violence goes against everything we believe in. We would rather exercise the rights guaranteed to us by the Constitution, drafted under the leadership of Dr B R Ambedkar, than resort to physical force," he noted.Dipke also criticised what he described as the government's contradictory approach to demonstrations, arguing that protests were treated as a democratic right when parties were in opposition but as a threat to public order when they came to power."Despite this, there are constant attempts to portray us as anarchists simply because we refuse to remain silent. But demanding answers from the govt is not anarchy, protesting against injustice on the streets is not anarchy, and questioning those who hold public office is certainly not anarchy," Dipke said.He maintained that an electoral mandate did not exempt the government from public scrutiny."We are not asking for privileges or special treatment. We are simply asking to exercise the rights that belong to every citizen of this Republic, irrespective of which party is in power... A govt that has been elected by the people is bound to listen to the people, not silence them. Democracy does not end once the votes have been counted," Dipke affirmed.ALSO READ: ‘True character of protests exposed’: Dharmendra Pradhan attacks Rahul Gandhi over regime change remark The NDMC announced that Central Park in Connaught Place would remain closed to the public on October 16 and 17 for "administrative reasons".Delhi Police said prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS were in force in Connaught Place and surrounding areas. The police also assured the Delhi High Court that all possible legal measures would be taken to address concerns surrounding the proposed CJP protest.Traffic movement on some roads in and around Connaught Place was expected to be affected from 3 pm on Friday, according to the Delhi Traffic Police.The proposed gathering has prompted heightened security and administrative restrictions in the area, with police warning that any march or assembly held in violation of the prohibitory orders could lead to legal action.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke served notice barring him from holding Tiranga march. Central Park in Connaught Place closed, traffic restrictions announced. Police warned that proceeding with the proposed gathering could invite legal action.

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Friday criticised the directive asking actor Imran Khan to leave India, saying it was beginning to feel as though protesting in the country had become a crime.“I read somewhere that Imran Khan was born in America. NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK. He claimed that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position. Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, will be held on October 6.

Article Title: Ajay Devgn’s Mumbai bungalow faces BMC action over unauthorised construction
Article Text:
BMC has rejected the owners' response regarding the ongoing construction at the Juhu bungalow owned by Ajay Devgn

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the decision to stop construction at Ajay Devgn bungalow was justified? Yes, they followed the rules No, it seems too harsh 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: The BMC has rejected the owners’ reply and deemed ongoing construction at actor Ajay Devgn’s Juhu bungalow unauthorised after they failed to submit documents establishing that the work had civic approval.The bungalow, located at Kapol Cooperative Housing Society in Juhu, is owned by Devgn and his mother, Veena Devgn.In a speaking order dated October 6, the BMC’s K/West ward office said the reply submitted on September 15 did not include documents establishing that the construction was authorised or a copy of permission granted by the competent authority.On September 10, the civic body had issued a stop-work notice under Section 354A of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, alleging unauthorised additions and alterations using Siporex blocks at CTS No. 841, Plot No. 10, Kapol CHS Ltd, on N S Road No. 11, JVPD, Vile Parle (West).The notice directed the owner or occupier to stop work immediately and submit the relevant permissions within 24 hours. It warned that the unauthorised structure and construction materials could be removed at the owner’s risk and cost if the directions were not followed. Police were also asked to monitor the site and remove those carrying out the work, if necessary.In its October 6 order, the BMC said permission from the competent authority was required for the ongoing construction. Since no supporting documents had been submitted, the owners’ reply could not be accepted and the work was deemed unauthorised.The order does not specify whether the civic body has since taken steps to remove the construction.
Article Summary: The bungalow, located at Kapol Cooperative Housing Society in Juhu, is owned by Devgn and his mother, Veena Devgn. BMC issued a stop-work notice under Section 354A of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act on September 10.

Article Title: 5 workers killed, 5 injured in explosion at chemical unit in Gujarat's Bharuch
Article Text:
Explosion at chemical manufacturing unit

(With Agency Inputs)





BHARUCH: At least five workers were killed and five others injured in an explosion at a pharmaceuticals factory in Sayakha GIDC area in Gujarat’s Bharuch, police said.The blast occurred around 10 pm on Friday during a hydrogenation process and triggered a leak of methylene dichloride (MDC) gas, officials said.Bharuch Sub-Divisional Magistrate Manisha Manani said SynZeal Pharmachem, which was set up in Saykha a year ago, manufactures pharmaceutical intermediates.The explosion, suspected to have occurred during the hydrogenation process, was powerful enough to rip apart the reactor tank, scattering machinery parts across the premises, she said.Superintendent of Police Akshyaraj Makwana said that five people died in the blast, while five others sustained injuries.The deceased were identified as Jaydeep Maheshbhai Patel and Bhavik Dilipkumar Vasava, both from Amod; Vrund Talaviya from Talala in Gir Somnath district; and Uttar Pradesh natives Aniket Harilal Gautam and Arjunkumar Ramsingh Gautam, he said.The injured workers were identified as Pavankumar Ramsingh Gautam, Mausamkumar Ramsevak Yadav, Shivdayal Ramavatar Yadav, Pratik Pravin Prajapati and Priyanshu Bahadurlal.The workers, who hail from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, are undergoing treatment, Makwana said.An official of the Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health (DISH) said the blast during the hydrogenation process triggered a leak of methylene dichloride (MDC) gas.Officials from the Gujarat Pollution Control Board, DISH and the police reached the site. The cause of the explosion is being investigated.
Article Summary: The blast occurred around 10 pm on Friday during a hydrogenation process and triggered a leak of methylene dichloride (MDC) gas, officials said. SynZeal Pharmachem, which was set up in Saykha a year ago, manufactures pharmaceutical intermediates.

Article Title: Iran broke? $25 billion oil loss, $350 million crypto frozen as militias send money back to IRGC, says US
Article Text:
Iran faces mounting financial pressure as US officials report $25 billion in lost oil revenue, $350 million in crypto frozen and militias sending funds back to the IRGC

Strait of Hormuz tensions

Iran is facing mounting financial pressure after nine months of war, with a US naval blockade costing it $25 billion in lost oil revenue and $350 million in cryptocurrency frozen, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM) chief Adm Brad Cooper.In a video message released on Friday, Cooper said Iran-backed groups across the region, including Hezbollah, Hamas and Shia militias in Iraq, were sending money back to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which has funded them for years."The financial strain on Iran's military has become so significant that there are reports about Iran-aligned militia groups across the region withholding payments for their soldiers in order to funnel money back to the IRGC, which also isn't paying its troops," Cooper said.He added that the Iranian government was withholding salaries, pensions and benefits from public sector workers, including internal security personnel and members of the IRGC.The financial squeeze comes as the Trump administration maintains a naval blockade and sanctions on Iran, hoping to push Tehran towards a deal that includes concessions on its nuclear programme. However, Iran has yet to respond to a US counterproposal aimed at ending the war.Cooper said CENTCOM and the US Treasury Department had also frozen $350 million in Iranian cryptocurrency in recent weeks. The naval blockade, meanwhile, had cost Tehran $25 billion in lost oil revenue, he said.Cooper attributed the recent increase in Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz to what he described as desperation within the IRGC.Despite the attacks, the strategic waterway remains open, he said, with 400 ships and 100 million barrels of oil moving through it over the past week.The US military has largely paused strikes on Iranian anti-ship missiles and attack drone launchers around the strait in recent weeks. A US official said the White House ordered the pause to avoid escalating the conflict ahead of the November midterm elections.US officials are concerned that continued attacks could discourage shipping companies from using the strait, reducing oil supplies and pushing up global prices. They also believe Iran is seeking to raise oil prices and increase pressure on US President Donald Trump ahead of the elections.Meanwhile, the White House and Qatari mediators are awaiting Tehran's response to Washington's counterproposal to end the war. A US official said the proposal was still under consideration in Tehran.Regional mediators have urged Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi not to delay the response until after the midterm elections, warning that there is no guarantee Trump would take a more conciliatory approach afterwards.
Article Summary: US officials report $25 billion in lost oil revenue, $350 million in crypto frozen and militias sending funds back to the IRGC. Iran-backed groups across the region, including Hezbollah, Hamas and Shia militias in Iraq, are sending money back to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which has funded them for years.

Article Title: 5 members of family, including 3 children, found dead in Greater Noida; food poisoning suspected
Article Text:
The deceased have been identified as Mahesh, his wife Lalita, and their children Laddu, Mishti, and Sakshat (Credits- Ramesh Sharma)

NOIDA: Five members of a family, including a couple and their three children aged between three and 11 years, were found dead under suspicious circumstances at their residence in Nagla Shri Padam village in Greater Noida’s Rabupura area on Saturday morning.Police suspect food poisoning as a possible cause, but the exact reason for the deaths is yet to be established.The deceased have been identified as Mahesh, 37, his wife Lalita, 35, and their children Laddu, 11, Mishti, seven, and Sakshat, three.According to police, information about the deaths was received at Rabupura police station on Saturday morning. Local police, senior officers, an ambulance and a team from the food safety department rushed to the spot.A forensic team and the police field unit inspected the scene and began collecting scientific evidence to establish the circumstances leading to the deaths.During the preliminary inquiry, neighbours and Mahesh’s mother reportedly told police that the family members had eaten noodles at night. All five were found dead the following morning. Frothing at the mouth was also reported, although officials have not yet confirmed its significance in determining the cause of death.Police said preliminary findings pointed to possible food poisoning. However, officials cautioned that the cause of death could be determined only after the postmortem examinations and other scientific investigations.The bodies are being sent for postmortem examinations after the completion of the necessary legal formalities. Further investigation is underway, and police said appropriate legal action would be taken based on the findings of the medical and forensic examinations.

Article Title: ‘He was under massive debt’: Shraddha Dubey recounts events before Lucknow bizman’s death
Article Text:
Shraddha Dubey has shared a second video asserting her innocence in the tragic case of Shiva Sharma's death

Claims Sharma was under financial stress

Denies torture, recounts events before death

Alleges Sharma’s mother assaulted her driver

Appeals to media, cites mental distress





LUCKNOW: A second video statement by Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma , has surfaced on social media. Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to her arrest.In the video, Dubey denies any role in Sharma’s death, describes it as a suicide and claims that he was under severe financial stress due to debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh. She has also appealed to the media to stop linking her to the case, saying she is under immense mental distress following the incident.Dubey says she had known Sharma for around four months and had been in a relationship with him for approximately two months. According to her, they had not spoken for several days before October 7, when Sharma allegedly contacted her driver through a tea vendor at the main crossing in Lucknow’s Kapurthala area.She claims Sharma was crying when he tried to reach her. Dubey says she called him twice before he called her around 2am and told her he was coming to meet her. He later arrived in his BMW. According to her account, he had consumed alcohol before they met.Dubey says they then went to Pedalers Cafe, where Sharma ordered matcha for her and her driver, along with juice for himself. She claims they later returned home, with Sharma driving her car and her driver driving Sharma’s BMW.Dubey alleges that Sharma had debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh and frequently received calls from creditors when they were together. She claims he had told her that he might take his own life if he failed to repay the money, although she says she did not take his statements seriously at the time.Dubey says she has screenshots of their conversations that she intends to share. She also claims Sharma’s mobile phone has been handed over to the police and that an examination of his call detail records could help establish the nature of the calls he received from creditors and shed light on the circumstances leading to his death.Her claims about Sharma’s debts and state of mind have not been independently verified.Dubey denies that Sharma was subjected to torture or abuse while he was with her. She says Sharma’s friends, whom she identifies as Ashwini Mishra and Harsh, visited them on October 8 and that their interactions were normal.She also says her sister visited her home that day to discuss arrangements for Navratri. According to Dubey, her sister barely knew Sharma and had no connection with the circumstances surrounding his death.Recounting the events of October 9, Dubey says she and Sharma woke up and went to the drawing room to have tea. Sharma then went to the washroom but closed the main entrance door, which she claims was unusual.Dubey says she became suspicious because of his earlier statements about his financial difficulties and asked her sister to check on him. However, she claims Sharma jumped from the balcony before her sister could open the door.Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment near Balu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area on October 9.Dubey claims Sharma’s mother arrived at the hospital after being informed of the incident and assaulted her driver. She says the incident would have been captured on hospital CCTV cameras.She further alleges that Sharma’s family accused her and others of murder without establishing the circumstances surrounding his death. Dubey says CCTV footage, call records and other evidence should be examined to determine what happened.These claims form part of Dubey’s account and have not been independently corroborated.Towards the end of the video, Dubey appeals to the media not to circulate rumours or repeatedly link her to the murder allegations. She says her deteriorating health and mental state prevented her from speaking immediately after the incident.She adds that she is grieving the loss of someone close to her and claims that continued harassment could push her towards suicide.Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of three people in connection with Sharma’s death: Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey, and Tanveer Ali, alias Danish, reportedly Dubey’s driver.The investigation into Sharma’s death is continuing. Dubey’s claims about suicide, financial distress and the events leading up to Sharma’s fall remain to be examined by investigators against CCTV footage, call detail records, witness accounts and other available evidence.
Article Summary: Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment near Balu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area on October 9. A second video statement by Shraddha Dubey, who is wanted in connection with the death, has surfaced on social media. Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to her arrest. Dubey claims Sharma had debts of Rs 15 lakh to Rs 20 lakh and frequently received calls from creditors when they were together.
